none_means: No qualifying prior reference verified; not a proof of novelty.

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of a possibly nonconvex C³ function f:E→ℝ, with f(x₀)−inf f≤Δ. No convexity assumption is imposed.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Oracle 0 returns the exact gradient together with the function value at any queried point, independently of call index and seed.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: Exact function values are bundled with gradients in oracle 0; each bundled evaluation counts as one call.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ThirdDerivativeSmoothNonconvex.lean: spec.Reply and spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: execute and _run.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Oracle 1 returns the exact full Hessian as a continuous linear operator. Hessian calls and value/gradient calls have separate fixed budgets. No third-derivative oracle is supplied.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ThirdDerivativeSmoothNonconvex.lean: spec.numOracles, spec.Reply and spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: execute.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its induced norm; no dimension bound is specified.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The third derivative is globally L₃-Lipschitz in operator norm. Only the initial Hessian is norm-bounded: ‖∇²f(x₀)‖≤H₀. Global gradient or Hessian Lipschitz bounds are not assumed. E, x₀, L₃, Δ, H₀ and ε are public; f is hidden. Parameters satisfy L₃>0, Δ>0, H₀≥0 and ε>0.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ThirdDerivativeSmoothNonconvex.lean: Params, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.valid and spec.admissible.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: Return one point x∈E satisfying ‖∇f(x)‖≤ε; the criterion uses the unsquared norm.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The returned point must satisfy the gradient-norm criterion almost surely under the joint algorithm and oracle seed law, within the separate fixed oracle budgets.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: An established higher-order smooth nonconvex stationarity formulation with exact derivative information, an initial objective-gap bound, and separately counted first- and second-order evaluations.
